key_insight: MLExpert proposes a generalist agentic model for autonomous machine learning engineering, aiming to let an LLM not just assist with ML tasks but orchestrate and improve them end-to-end. The paper frames this as a practical step toward AI systems that can iteratively build better AI systems.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of automating long-horizon machine learning engineering workflows, where many steps, experiments, and decisions must be coordinated without constant human intervention. It targets the gap between LLM assistance and truly autonomous ML system development.
method: Uses a workflow-driven machine learning engineering setup to manage complex, long-running experimentation loops.
Introduces model-directed interaction, allowing the model to autonomously plan, act, and adapt across ML engineering tasks.
Positions MLExpert as a generalist agentic model that can support multiple phases of autonomous AI system development.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this points toward faster experimentation and reduced manual effort in building, tuning, and improving ML systems. It also suggests a path toward more autonomous AI engineering pipelines that can scale beyond one-off assistance.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing autonomous ML engineering workflow from problem setup to model improvement
Agent loop illustration with plan → act → evaluate → refine
Comparison chart of human-driven vs model-directed MLE workflows
Icon set for experiments, orchestration, feedback, and optimization
paper_title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
paper_authors: Shangheng Du, Jinxin Shi, Shuaiyu Zhang, Yiming Wu, Junpeng Zhao
